newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GERMAN FOUR-WAY TITLE BATTLE HOTS UP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMAN FOUR-WAY TITLE BATTLE HOTS UP.

text.p: Germany is staging one of the closest league title battles in Europe.
Just two points separate the top four teams -- Dortmund, Bayern Munich, VfB Stuttgart and Bayer Leverkusen -- after weekend matches.
Manchester United, Juventus and Real Madrid stayed ahead of their championship rivals in England, Italy and Spain respectively.
GERMANY
VfB Stuttgart intensified the race for the championship when they blasted four goals past leaders Borussia Dortmund.
A 44th minute penalty from Bulgarian Krasimir Balakov and goals from Dutchman Frank Verlaat, Brazilian striker Giovane Elber and Croat Zvonimir Soldo helped Stuttgart to a 4-1 win.

Defending champions Dortmund, who went ahead in Stuttgart with an eighth minute goal from Germany defender Stefan Reuter, stayed top but Bayern drew level on points after a 3-0 victory over Schalke in Munich's Olympic stadium.
Stuttgart are now just two points behind in third place, ahead of Bayer Leverkusen on goal difference. Leverkusen won 1-0 at home against promoted Arminia Bielefeld.
ENGLAND

Manchester United stretched their lead at the top of the premier league to three points with a 2-0 win over in-form Sheffield Wednesday as title rivals Liverpool were held 1-1 at lowly Nottingham Forest.
Third-placed Arsenal drew level with Liverpool on points thanks to a 2-0 win at Southampton.

United went ahead with a first-half Andy Cole goal but had to work hard to contain a Wednesday side which had lost just one of their last 20 league games. Czech Karel Poborsky hammered in the second after an hour.
Robbie Fowler gave Liverpool the ideal start with a goal after just four minutes, but Forest levelled after half-an-hour following a mistake by David James.
The Liverpool goalkeeper saw his punched clearance sail straight back over his head and into the net via the boot of midfielder Ian Woan.
ITALY
Parma striker Enrico Chiesa dented Internazionale's hopes of a place in the European Cup next season while Juventus, the holders, beat Roma to stay five points clear at the top of serie A.
Chiesa's 22nd minute goal, a twist followed by an unstoppable left-footer, gave Parma a 1-0 home victory to establish them as the clear second force in Italy.

Juventus, who won 3-0 in Turin thanks to two goals from stand-in striker Christian Vieri, have 48 points while Parma, who finished with 10 men after midfielder Dino Baggio was sent off in the 79th minute for two bookings, have 43.
Inter total 38 and as much chance of finishing second, and thereby clinching a European Cup place, as Parma do of overtaking Juventus and winning the title.
AC Milan, struggling in 12th place before Saturday's match, overcame Cup Winners' Cup hopefuls Fiorentina 2-0 to leapfrog over them, Napoli and Lazio and move ninth.
SPAIN
Substitute Emmanuel Amunike kept Barcelona in the league title race with an 82nd minute winner at Logrones.

The 1-0 result left Barcelona six points adrift of leaders Real Madrid, who play at Real Sociedad on Monday. Coach Bobby Robson's side clung on to second place on goal difference ahead of Betis, who had thrashed Rayo Vallecano 4-0 earlier.
Amunike, who has struggled since signing form Sporting Lisbon, headed home his first goal for his new club from a free-kick by midfielder Ivan de la Pena.

Betis kept up their strong challenge thanks to a second successive league hat-trick by Alfonso Perez, who was given a standing ovation by Rayo Vallecano fans after being substituted towards the end of their side's 4-0 defeat.
FRANCE
Second-placed Paris St Germain undermined their league title chances by slumping to a 1-0 defeat at lowly Le Havre, leaving them seven points behind Monaco.
The Paris club were lucky to see Teddy Bertin miss a penalty after a foul by goalkeeper Bernard Lama on Le Havre striker Roger Boli three minutes from halftime.
But with 14 minutes remaining, another offence on Boli, this time by midfielder Benoit Cauet, gave Bertin another chance from the penalty spot which he converted.

Sylvain Legwinski scored twice to help leaders Monaco win 3-0 at Rennes, and Strasbourg moved up one place to third by winning 1-0 at former Eurpean champions Marseille thanks to a Pascal Nouma goal in the 51st minute.
